newsitem.title: USA: PSA seeks lower threshold for private placements.
newsitem.headline: PSA seeks lower threshold for private placements.

text.p: Underwriters of private placement offerings should be able to solicit qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) with assets of $25 to $50 million, not the current threshold of $100 million, the U.S. Public Securities Association said on Monday.
In a release, the PSA said success of the Securities and Exchange Commission's Rule 144a prompted its call for expansion and revision.
"Current restrictions unnecessarily burden the underwriter by imposing a requirement to determine, before the solicitation process begins, the QIB status of everyone they contact, the PSA said.
"Moreover, inadvertent conversations with non-qualified buyers could force underwriters to cancel the offering," the trade association added.
The PSA's recommendation for changes in Rule 144a was included as part of its call for select modification of the SEC's securities regulatory system.
